title: Smartphone 3D reconstruction measures eyelid ptosis in a prospective multicenter study
summary: The Digital Rulers of Ptosis system reconstructs the eye region in 3D from a 10-second smartphone video to measure marginal reflex distance 1 (MRD1) and levator function. Across 952 participants (1904 eyes) at 5 hospitals, mean absolute error against specialist measurement was 0.52 mm for MRD1 and 0.95 mm for levator function, with AUC 0.97 for diagnosing ptosis and 0.98 for identifying the surgical approach. Among 206 surgical participants (248 eyes), 3-month recurrence was 7.3%; the authors state that further studies are needed to evaluate clinical impact.
ai_technology: Neural-network 3D reconstruction and landmark detection from smartphone video
organization: Sun Yat-sen University; State Key Laboratory of Ophthalmology; Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, Sun Yat-sen University

evidence.tested: Prospective 5-hospital measurement study against same-day oculoplastic specialist assessment (952 participants), with 3-month postoperative follow-up.
evidence.unknown: Clinical impact not evaluated; specialist measurement is the reference standard; recurrence rate is compared with published rates only; abstract and PMC full text reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Neural-network 3D reconstruction and landmark detection from smartphone video yield eyelid measurements and classification.
